## Intent
Hypothesis: a Halide-expressible branchless blend with per-particle hash RNG can approach the streaming ceiling on this particle workload.

## Cache saturation
The L1d spill at N≈963 falls below the smallest measured point (N=4000). At N=4000 (L2-resident), ns/p is 10.68–11.76; by N=65000 (just past the L2→DRAM spill at N≈61680) cost FALLS to 7.69–7.99 and stays FLAT through N=4M (7.75–8.00). No cache-spill knee appears at the L2→DRAM boundary—cost drops rather than rises, indicating per-frame setup overhead (the `bl _halide_b1` call and 0x3f0-byte stack frame) dominates at small N and amortizes by N=65000. Death rate slightly lowers the floor at q=0.25 (7.69 vs 7.99 at N=65000) without reshaping the N-curve.

## Bandwidth
Peak achieved is 8.84 GB/s at N=65000, q=0.25—35% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling. At q=0.01 the peak is 8.56 GB/s (34%). The algo is overhead-bound at N=4000 (5.78–6.37 GB/s), transitioning to compute-bound by N=65000 where bandwidth plateaus and never rises with N. It is never bandwidth-bound: the flat 8.5–8.8 GB/s profile from N=65000 to N=4M, well below ceiling, rules out a memory-wall limitation.

## Assembly
The compiler did not vectorize the particle loop. Only 2 vector-suffixed instructions appear—both `movi.2d` for zero-init. All floating-point is scalar: `fmul` on s-registers, `fadd s4`, `fsub s4`, `fcmp s6,s2`, `fcvtzs w12,s6`. Each particle is loaded scalar-wise (`ldp s4,s5`, `ldp s6,s7`, `ldr s16`) and processed individually. The 18 `csel` instructions implement the branchless blend; 16 `strb` stores with `csel`-based saturation to 0xff perform byte-granular scatter into the pixel buffer. This scalar per-particle codegen with byte-granular scatter explains why bandwidth stalls at 35% of ceiling—no SIMD amortization and `strb` writes cannot stream.

## Verdict
Refuted—the algo never exceeds 8.84 GB/s (35% of the 25.22 GB/s ceiling), and scalar codegen (2 vector instructions total, all FP on s-registers, 16 `strb` byte stores) confirms compute-bound behavior. The flat ns/p of 7.69–8.00 from N=65000 through N=4M shows no approach to the streaming ceiling at any death rate or problem size.
